context_requirements: Cells must be actively cycling with intact cell-cycle checkpoints and/or mitotic machinery.
TP53 status influences the transcriptional output: wild-type TP53 can drive CDKN1A and GADD45 induction, while TP53-mutant lines may rely more on p53-independent arrest or apoptosis.
RB-proficient cells can show stronger E2F-dependent repression of replication genes.
Rapidly dividing lines with high baseline proliferation markers give larger decreases in cell-cycle genes.
falsifiers: No decrease in proliferation-associated landmark genes such as CCNA2, CCNB1, CDK1, CDC20, BIRC5, AURKA, AURKB, PLK1, TOP2A, MCM3, PCNA, UBE2C, KIF20A, or NUSAP1 at 6 h or 24 h in any responsive line.
No induction of CDKN1A, GADD45A, GADD45B, SFN, SESN1, or other p53/p21-associated genes at 6 h or 24 h.
A purely generic stress signature with no cell-cycle gene changes at either time point.
Strong and selective induction of interferon, heat-shock, or unfolded-protein-response programs without any cell-cycle transcriptional effect.
Identical transcriptional response in all nine lines with no relationship to proliferation rate or TP53/RB status.
